findings.description: Critical: Step 11.5 embeds `/audit-choices "$CHANGE_ID" --run-id "$RUN_ID"` inside a ```bash``` command substitution (`audit_output=$(/audit-choices ...)`). `/audit-choices` is a skill slash-command, not a filesystem binary: running the fence as shell yields `No such file or directory` (exit 127), so every run takes `SKIP_REASON="audit dispatch failed"` and never produces or commits a ledger. Sibling skills are invoked from bash via `python3 "<skill-base-dir>/../..."`; skill dispatch elsewhere in this file is agent prose/`Task(...)`, not `$(/skill-name ...)`. The prose says "Dispatch the audit-choices skill" while the fence treats it as a shell CLI, so the intended executor is ambiguous at the point of use.
findings.resolution: Split Step 11.5 into (1) an agent-level instruction to dispatch `/audit-choices $CHANGE_ID --run-id ...` (or an equivalent provider-neutral dispatch), then (2) a pure-bash block that only does the F2/F6 existence check, comparison, orphan cleanup, and commit/restore — with WARNING detection based on files/driver output the shell can actually observe.

findings.description: Critical: The partial-pair guard only checks that both paths are non-empty (`[ -s "$JSON_PATH" ]` / `[ -s "$MD_PATH" ]`). `write_ledger_pair` writes `choices.json` then `choices.md` as separate operations; on a re-audit, an interruption after the JSON rewrite leaves new non-empty JSON beside the still-present prior `choices.md`. Both `-s` checks pass, the F2 compare reports `changed`, and the step `git add`s/`git commit`s a mismatched pair (fresh JSON + stale markdown). First-audit half-writes (JSON only) are handled; the re-audit half-write shape that F6’s non-atomic write implies is not.
findings.resolution: Treat a re-audit as partial unless `choices.md` is demonstrably rendered from the fresh JSON (e.g. rewrite/compare mtime after JSON, or always restore both paths and skip whenever the pair was not produced in one successful `write_ledger_pair` call). Extend the orphan-cleanup behavioral test with a tracked pair whose JSON is rewritten and whose MD is left stale.

findings.description: Critical: `load_needs_user_entries` does `entries = doc.get("entries", [])` and then iterates. When the key is present with JSON `null`, `.get` returns `None` (the default is not used), and `for e in entries` raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`. That violates F3’s "never raises" / always-exit-0 contract and would make both gate hooks fail instead of rendering the empty forms. Unreadable JSON is caught; this readable-but-malformed shape is not.
findings.resolution: After loading the doc, coerce with `entries = doc.get("entries") if isinstance(doc.get("entries"), list) else []` (and keep the existing try/except). Add a unit test that writes `{"entries": null}` and asserts exit 0 with empty stdout.

findings.description: Critical: In validate-feature Step 11, `CHOICES_LINES` is assigned only in the `else` branch (ledger present). Step 12’s unquoted heredoc expands `$CHOICES_LINES` unconditionally. Under `set -u` (nounset), a no-ledger run aborts with `CHOICES_LINES: unbound variable` while writing `validation-report.md` — a new failure mode on the path that should print `○ Choices: no ledger` and continue. Reproduced: `set -u` + unset `CHOICES_LINES` in `<<EOF` exits 127.
findings.resolution: Initialize `CHOICES_LINES=""` before the `if`, or use `${CHOICES_LINES-}` / `${CHOICES_LINES:-}` in the heredoc (and prefer a quoted heredoc body for the static parts).

findings.description: Nit: Faithfulness to F2 is pinned only by prose assertions (`"entries" array`, `header.schema_version`, "commit nothing") in `test_states_f2_commit_rule`. No test extracts or executes the comparison Python the way `test_orphan_cleanup_behavior` extracts the orphan-cleanup snippet. A rewrite that compared the whole document (or subtracted only `generated_at`/`run_id`) while leaving those comment strings would keep the suite green but would never skip commits, because `header.git_sha` and `audited_range` move every run — the exact failure F2 was written to prevent.
findings.resolution: Extract the comparison snippet from Step 11.5 and run it against fixture ledgers: no HEAD revision → `new`; same entries/schema_version with different git_sha/audited_range/generated_at → `unchanged`; different entries → `changed`.

findings.description: Nit: `test_workflow_hooks.py` never asserts that Step 11.5’s audit invocation is something a shell (or an unambiguous agent step) can actually run successfully. Finding 1’s `$(/audit-choices ...)` form would not fail any current hook test, so skill-workflow.8’s success path (audit runs and may commit) is unpinned while only the skip/orphan branches are covered.
findings.resolution: After fixing the invocation shape, assert the fence does not call a root-path `/audit-choices` binary and that skill dispatch is specified outside command substitution (or that a real `python3 "<skill-base-dir>/../audit-choices/scripts/run_audit.py"` path is used if that becomes the design).

findings.description: none: F2’s comparison Python correctly builds `(entries, header.schema_version)` and treats a missing `git show HEAD:…` revision as `new` (always commit). That matches design F2 and would skip only when entries and schema_version are unchanged despite volatile header/range fields.
findings.resolution: Keep this comparison shape; add an executable pin as in finding 5 so it cannot regress silently.

findings.description: none: The F6 orphan-cleanup loop decides per path via `git ls-files --error-unmatch` whether to `git checkout --` or `rm -f`, and `test_orphan_cleanup_behavior` executes that snippet against both untracked and tracked partial-pair fixtures — correctly guarding the earlier bug where an unconditional `rm -f` deleted a pair the checkout had just restored.
findings.resolution: Keep the if/else per-path cleanup; extend coverage for the stale-MD re-audit shape (finding 2).

findings.description: none: Both gate hooks invoke the reader via `python3 "<skill-base-dir>/../audit-choices/scripts/needs_user.py"`, and `_assert_reader_invoked_skill_relative` fails on a bare command or repo-root `skills/...` path — so runtime mirrors under `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/` stay resolvable.
